d:
This gallery contains various assets from the free demo of the NSFW point-and-click adventure game Crooked Knobs. Note that the demo takes place BEFORE the actual final game, and its story scenario is not covered there, this demo is a completely separate experience. (which is my main motivation for uploading this, this will all probably not appear in the final game, only in this demo) You also don't need to play it to understand the final game, its just a preview of the game's basic systems. To whit, the protagonist of the full game is the fox detective, but in this demo you only play as the his superior, Detective Lance. The game(s) contain bisexual content.

As for the gallery's contents, its rather complicated. None of the animations here were originally gifs. They were either a spritesheet sequence to be animated in-game, or a webm file played mid-game, I tried to convert them all to gifs that match the animation's native framerate as best as I could (though I'm an amateur at that, so I just used ezgif.com). A lot of the webm files had a solid black background that I couldn't work around, or rather, the conversion process turned the background completely black and I couldn't work around it and make it look good at the same time. (this is most obvious in jacky's portion of the gallery).

Not EVERY animation is here, the ending sequence I was not able to convert as it was all black sprites on a black background. I couldn't separate it at my skill level. Its not terribly exciting, you're not missing much.

I organized the files by characters, and more or less thei importance and order you meet them in. So, its the two detectives, the LeTits nightclub staff (Kaguya, Bora, Etna, Ziran, Cassius, the nightclub guests, Geniou), Jacky, Gamon, and lastly Dyabal. (note, Dyabal's sprites are recolored in-game to appear completely black/obscured, he makes an appearance in the final game) In Jacky's section, you may notice several half-body sprites, these are used for the final confrontation at the end of the demo. There are several unused animations, so I don't have a frame of reference for their framerate and as such I just included the static sprites that ARE used as well. The art at the end of the gallery are in-game cgs, old art made by an artist named Jedader, and the arts used in the cardgame against Jacky.

pg 2-33: the detectives and the demo's intro sequence. The animation is actually 4 webms played on top of each other, not 4 gifs.

pg 34-65: The LeTits Nightclub staff and their sex scenes.

pg 66-74: Cassius' strip show audience. (Cassius' animation is supposed to be on a stage between them)

pg 75-81: Geniou, the LeTits nightclub security.

pg 82-94: the other guests present at the nightclub. They're not terribly important. (Ty's animation is supposed to be looking at Jame).

(note, the Staff and other guests area all cameos, the in-game guestbook shows who owns them).

pg 95-141: Jacky Jones, the final confrontation and card game arts and animations. Note: the animations of 99-101 were recorded from the in-game gallery, due to them actually being a series of webms that were originally black sprites that I could not seperate from the webm's background. The animations of 97-105 are all parts of the same sequence. The cardgame win screens actually have more visual elements, but I couldn't be bothered to stitch them all together. The animation of Jacky's clothes is irritatingly actually a seperate webm, not a sprite sequence, so I DID try to seperate the animation from the background and combine it with the ending climax, but it did not turn out very well.

pg 142-167: Gamon, and his animations during the final confrontation against Jacky. His "cum prank" animation is actually an easter egg, there's a small chance of it happening when he spies on Jacky's card for you. The "big/true" Gamon does not have a full version in the game's files. The talking versions of Gamon's confrontation animations are supposed to have a transparent shadowy double, but it doesn't show up in the gifs I made.

pg 168-174: Dyabal, who only shows up in the demo's secret ending. As a reminder, his sprites only show as completely black in game.

pg 175-178: In-game cgs of plot-important evidence.

pg 179-185: old art made by an artist named Jedader, used as cameos.

pg 186-203: The arts used for the cards in the cardgame at the end.
